documents.unit: Office of the Provost (Joint University Curriculum Committee)
documents.title: Syllabus Statement Options for Generative AI
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule; it says "you may choose one of three options" (comprehensive use with attribution, use only within instructor parameters, or discouraged/not permitted unless stated) and calls them "templates that can be customized". Because it offers tiers and hands the decision to instructors, the stance is delegates.
tiers: Use only within instructor-given parameters per assignment, with attribution
Strongly discouraged or not permitted unless explicitly stated by the instructor
documents.summary: A provost-approved set of three customizable syllabus statements on generative AI, from open use with attribution to discouragement or prohibition. A note to instructors warns that prohibition may be unenforceable, drives use underground and raises equity issues, and the page records the committee and provost approvals and an October 2025 update.

units.why: The page says who adopted the statements and when: 'the Provost approved the JUCC' recommendation'. This records how the policy was made, so it is P84 (process and date of adoption), informational.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P84/informs/admin; they differed on phase (A general, B before-course) and anchor. Source: 'the JUCC recommended ... Provost approved the JUCC's recommendation' describes adoption, an institutional set-up act, so before-course. B's dated normalization matches the passage.
units.anchor: the Provost approved the JUCC's recommendation
units.frag_end: the Provost approved the JUCC's recommendation.
units.policy: The Joint University Curriculum Committee recommended the syllabus statement options on May 16th, 2024, and the Provost approved the recommendation on July 15th, 2024.

units.why: The statements were revised in October 2025 ('recommended updates to the USF syllabus statements'), which shows the policy is revised over time. P54 (revisit regularly) fits partly because it reports one revision rather than a commitment to review.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P54/informs/admin/over-time and noted it records one revision, not a review cycle. Source says the JUCC recommended updates on October 16th, 2025 and the Provost approved them; B's normalization is faithful, so kept with B's fit_note.
units.anchor: the JUCC recommended updates to the USF syllabus statements
units.policy: The JUCC recommended updates to the USF syllabus statements and customization guide on October 16th, 2025, and the Provost approved them.
units.fit_note: Reports a past revision (Oct 2025) rather than promising regular review.

units.why: 'you may choose one of three options' gives instructors a menu of named statements ranging from comprehensive use to prohibition. That is a set of tiers (P05), addressed to instructors as a permission.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P05, instructor, may, before-course. Source: 'you may choose one of three options'. They differed only on topics and on policy (A null, B normalized); a normalized policy is kept because the anchor omits the instructor addressee.
units.anchor: you may choose one of three options to address the use of generative AI tools
units.policy: Instructors may choose one of three syllabus statement options to address generative AI use.

units.why: 'These statements are templates that can be customized to fit your course context.' The university supplies template syllabus statements for instructors to adopt and adapt. That is P110 (sample syllabus language); P04 does not fit because the sentence does not say who decides whether AI is allowed.
units.resolution_why: A coded P04 (customization is the delegation); B coded P110. The source calls the options 'templates', which is the P110 definition (institution supplies templates for instructors to adopt). Who decides AI use is covered by the three-options and discretion units, so P110.
units.anchor: These statements are templates that can be customized to fit your course context.

units.why: Instructors are told to read the customization guide 'before choosing a statement', a pointer to further guidance (P115) with a 'should' force.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P115/should/instructor/before-course. Source: 'please reference the Faculty Considerations ... before choosing a statement'. B's normalization states the 'should' force and addressee, kept.
units.anchor: Faculty Considerations for Syllabus Statement Customization
units.policy: Instructors should reference the Faculty Considerations for Syllabus Statement Customization before choosing a statement.

units.why: The statements are 'already embedded in your syllabus' in Simple Syllabus, a template-distribution mechanism, so P110.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P110/informs/instructor/before-course; source: 'the three statements are already embedded in your syllabus and ready to edit' in Simple Syllabus. No disagreement.
units.anchor: the three statements are already embedded in your syllabus
units.frag_start: If you are using Simple Syllabus

units.why: Option 1 says 'the comprehensive use of generative AI tools is permitted'. It is a default-permit stance for the course, hence P02 with permit.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P02/may/student/permit; they differed only on anchor and wording (A policy null, B normalized). Source: 'In this course at the instructor's discretion, the comprehensive use of generative AI tools is permitted with appropriate attribution.' B's normalization is faithful to the sentence.
units.anchor: the comprehensive use of generative AI tools is permitted with appropriate attribution
units.policy: In this course, at the instructor's discretion, the comprehensive use of generative AI tools is permitted with appropriate attribution.

units.why: 'at the instructor's discretion' leaves the use of AI to the instructor, which is P04.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded the clause 'at the instructor's discretion' separately; coder A folded it into the Option 1 permission. The clause is a distinct rule (who decides), so it is kept as a separate P04 unit with informs modality. Anchor lengthened so it is a full phrase.
units.anchor: In this course at the instructor's discretion
units.policy: Whether comprehensive generative AI use is permitted is at the instructor's discretion.

units.why: Option 1 conditions the permission on 'appropriate attribution', a disclosure requirement (P24). I chose P24 over P02 because this unit is the attribution duty, while the permission is coded separately.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P24/must/student/during-work/require. Source: 'permitted with appropriate attribution'. The attribution duty is coded apart from the permission (unit above). Normalized wording kept close to the source; B's fit_note kept.
units.anchor: permitted with appropriate attribution
units.policy: Generative AI use under the first statement must come with appropriate attribution.
units.fit_note: Does not say what the attribution must contain.

units.why: 'in alignment with the USF Honor Code, students must present work that is authentically their own' states that submitted work must be the student's own, which is P29.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P29/must/student/general. They differed on unit_stance (A neutral, B restrict). Source: 'In alignment with the USF Honor Code, students must present work that is authentically their own' does not mention AI itself, so it takes no position on AI use: neutral. It repeats in all three statements; coded once.
units.anchor: students must present work that is authentically their own
units.policy: In alignment with the USF Honor Code, students must present work that is authentically their own.

units.why: Option 2 allows AI 'only ... within the parameters provided by the instructor, specific to each assignment'. The rule is set per assignment by the instructor (P04), and it is narrow, so unit_stance is restrict.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P04/may/student/during-work/restrict and agreed on all codes. Source: 'only permitted within the parameters provided by the instructor, specific to each assignment, with appropriate attribution'. The per-assignment rule is set by the instructor (P04); attribution is coded separately. B's normalization and fit_note kept.
units.anchor: only permitted within the parameters provided by the instructor
units.frag_start: In this course, the use of
units.policy: In this course, generative AI use is only permitted within the parameters provided by the instructor, specific to each assignment, with appropriate attribution.
units.fit_note: Also makes permitted use conditional on attribution and narrower than the default.

units.why: Option 2 also requires 'appropriate attribution' for permitted uses, a disclosure requirement (P24).
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P24/must/student/during-work/require. Source: 'specific to each assignment, with appropriate attribution'. Wording adjusted to state the duty plainly.
units.anchor: specific to each assignment, with appropriate attribution
units.frag_start: In this course, the use of
units.policy: Generative AI use under the second statement must come with appropriate attribution.

units.why: Option 3 says use is 'strongly discouraged' in one form of the statement, discouraging without a formal ban (P03).
units.resolution_why: A coded one P06 unit with a fit note that the wording may be mere discouragement; B split into P03 (discouraged) and P06 (not permitted). The source offers the two wordings as alternatives and the note says to choose one, so each is a distinct policy variant. Both are kept: P03 for the 'strongly discouraged' variant, P06 for the 'not permitted' variant. Modality should-not for discouraged.
units.anchor: strongly discouraged or not permitted unless explicitly stated by the instructor
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI tools is
units.frag_end: unless explicitly stated by the instructor.
units.policy: Use of generative AI tools is strongly discouraged unless explicitly stated by the instructor.
units.fit_note: Template offers 'strongly discouraged' or 'not permitted' as alternative wordings.

units.why: 'not permitted unless explicitly stated by the instructor' fixes the fallback: AI is off unless the instructor says otherwise, which is P06 (default rule with silence), and it is a restrictive stance.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P06/must-not/student/course-start/restrict for the fallback 'not permitted unless explicitly stated by the instructor'. B's normalization is faithful, kept. A's fit_note (it can be soft discouragement) is addressed by the separate P03 unit.
units.anchor: not permitted unless explicitly stated by the instructor
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI tools is
units.policy: Generative AI use is not permitted unless explicitly stated by the instructor.
units.fit_note: Template also allows the softer 'strongly discouraged' wording, coded as a separate P03 unit.

units.why: 'If the use of generative AI tools is permitted at any interval in the course, specific instructions must be followed' puts the duty on students to follow the rules given where AI is allowed (P78).
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P78/must/student/during-work; they differed on unit_stance (A restrict, B permit). Source: 'If the use of generative AI tools is permitted at any interval in the course, specific instructions must be followed' allows use with conditions, which the codebook calls permit. A's note about P08 staging is not needed: nothing says permission grows over time.
units.anchor: specific instructions must be followed
units.frag_start: If the use of generative AI
units.policy: If generative AI use is permitted at any interval in the course, specific instructions must be followed.

units.why: 'please ask your instructor to clarify any questions you may have' tells students to ask when unsure, which is P10.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P10/should/student/course-start. Source: 'please ask your instructor to clarify any questions you may have'. B's normalization kept.
units.anchor: please ask your instructor to clarify any questions you may have
units.policy: Students should ask their instructor to clarify any questions about the AI policy.

units.why: 'this policy may be different from other course AI policies' tells students one course's rule does not carry to others, which is P11.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P11/informs/student/course-start. Source: 'this policy may be different from other course AI policies'. No disagreement.
units.anchor: this policy may be different from other course AI policies
units.policy: This course's AI policy may be different from other courses' AI policies.

units.why: 'To mitigate risks associated with the use of generative AI, please review the Guidelines for Responsible Use' sends students to a further guidance document (P115) and frames it as risk reduction.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P115/should/student/course-start. Source: 'To mitigate risks associated with the use of generative AI, please review the Guidelines for Responsible Use ...'. B's 'should' normalization kept (the 'please' is a recommendation).
units.anchor: To mitigate risks associated with the use of generative AI
units.frag_end: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) at USF
units.policy: Students should review the Guidelines for Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) at USF to mitigate risks associated with generative AI use.

units.why: The note tells instructors "Do not include both" 'strongly discouraged' and 'not permitted' "as this will be confusing to students". It is advice on wording the rule clearly, closest to P66 (word the rules with care), though P66 is about explaining rules to students.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P66/instructor/before-course, with fit notes that it is about unambiguous wording. They differed on modality (A must-not, B should-not). Source: 'Please customize ... Do not include both' is a direct instruction, so must-not. P66 includes 'word the rules with care', so it is the nearest fit.
units.anchor: Do not include both, as this will be confusing to students
units.policy: Instructors must not include both 'strongly discouraged' and 'not permitted' in the third statement, as this will be confusing to students.
units.fit_note: The unit is about choosing one unambiguous wording for the statement, not explaining reasons or discussing AI with students.

units.why: The note admits the third statement 'may not be enforceable' and that prohibiting 'drives their use underground'. It acknowledges AI prohibition cannot be fully verified or controlled, so P82.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P82/informs/instructor/before-course. Source: 'it may not be enforceable. Be aware that prohibiting GenAI tools use or not providing clear expectations drives their use underground.' Both normalizations match; wording merged to follow the source.
units.anchor: it may not be enforceable
units.policy: The third syllabus statement option may not be enforceable, and prohibiting GenAI tools use or not providing clear expectations drives their use underground.

units.why: 'This presents a significant equity issue, privileging students who have more sophisticated language abilities and/or expertise with GenAI tools' is an argument that bans and unclear expectations are inequitable. It is a rationale given to instructors, so modality informs. P51 covers cost, access and alternatives, which this is not, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: A coded UNCOVERED; B coded P51 with a fit note that it is not about access. Source: equity harm arises from hidden use favoring skilled users, not from cost or tool access. P51's definition (free access, no paid tools, accommodations) does not say that, so UNCOVERED under constant comparison. Both coders' notes kept.
units.anchor: This presents a significant equity issue
units.frag_start: This presents a significant equity issue
units.policy: Banning AI or leaving expectations unclear presents a significant equity issue, privileging students with more sophisticated language abilities or expertise with GenAI tools.
units.fit_note: B's nearest type was P51; its fit note said equity here is advantage for skilled AI users under hidden use, not cost or access to tools.
units.uncovered_note: Warns instructors that banning AI or leaving expectations unclear is an equity problem because it favors students with stronger language skills or AI expertise.

units.why: The note says GenAI is 'increasingly embedded in a range of technologies' so students may not know when they use it. That addresses AI built into other tools (P07), as a consideration rather than a rule.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P07/informs/instructor/before-course with fit notes that the unit informs rather than regulates. Source: 'GenAI functionality, which is increasingly embedded in a range of technologies ... it may not always be apparent to students'. B's normalization is faithful, kept.
units.anchor: GenAI functionality, which is increasingly embedded in a range of technologies
units.frag_start: Also, be aware that GenAI tools
units.policy: GenAI functionality is increasingly embedded in a range of technologies, so it may not always be apparent to students when or if they are using GenAI tools.
units.fit_note: Informs instructors of embedded AI rather than regulating it.

units.why: 'This is an important consideration in terms of punitive consequences' follows the point that students may not know they use embedded GenAI. It asks instructors to weigh that before punishing. No type states this caution; P68 is about educative responses and P69 about evidence, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: A coded P68 (should) with a fit note that it does not prescribe educative responses; B coded UNCOVERED (informs). Source only says the point is 'an important consideration in terms of punitive consequences', and prescribes no educative response, so P68 would stretch. UNCOVERED with modality informs; A's fit note kept.
units.anchor: This is an important consideration in terms of punitive consequences
units.frag_start: In these situations, it may not
units.policy: When students may not know they are using embedded GenAI, this is an important consideration in terms of punitive consequences.
units.fit_note: A's nearest type was P68; the unit only asks instructors to weigh the difficulty of telling when AI is used before punishing; it does not prescribe educative responses.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should weigh that students may not realise they are using embedded AI before imposing punishment.

documents.title: DLI Generative AI Hub
documents.stance_why: The hub 'welcomes innovation' yet says users 'must follow' existing technology, security and AI guidelines; it sets no rule on students' use in courses and points instructors to syllabus statements. It sets no stance of its own on classroom use, so delegates.
documents.summary: An ITS hub page defining generative AI, framing the risks of data security, compliance, copyright and academic integrity, and listing training, consultation and syllabus resources. It sets data-classification limits by tool type and requires technology assessment and the use of the university's responsible-use guidelines, which are not in the saved text.

units.why: The hub defines GenAI as 'a branch of artificial intelligence that specializes in creating new content', which sets what the term covers (P61).
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P61/informs/all/general. Source: 'GenAI is a branch of artificial intelligence that specializes in creating new content.' Topics differed (A policy-evolution, B ethics-bias-environment); neither fits well, policy-evolution kept.
units.anchor: GenAI is a branch of artificial intelligence that specializes in creating new content

units.why: 'GenAI has the potential to revolutionize the way we work and learn' names a benefit of AI without making a rule, which is P87.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded 'GenAI has the potential to revolutionize the way we work and learn'. It is a real statement of AI's benefit with no rule: P87, informs, unit_stance encourage. Kept.
units.anchor: GenAI has the potential to revolutionize the way we work and learn

units.why: 'USF welcomes innovation by exploring the exciting possibilities of GenAI tools, but there are important considerations ... including information security and data privacy, compliance, copyright, and academic integrity' is a university-wide framing statement of purpose and principles, P56.
units.resolution_why: A coded P02 with a fit note that the welcome is institutional exploration, not a student-use default; B coded P56. Source: 'USF welcomes innovation by exploring the exciting possibilities of GenAI tools' is an institutional posture, not a rule for student use, so P56 (institution-wide framework) fits and P02 does not. unit_stance encourage (A) over permit (B) because it welcomes rather than permits.
units.anchor: USF welcomes innovation by exploring the exciting possibilities of GenAI tools
units.fit_note: Welcome is directed at institutional exploration of GenAI tools, not a default rule for student use (A's note).

units.why: The page lists "information security and data privacy, compliance, copyright, and academic integrity" as the considerations when using these tools. It names the principles behind the guidance, so P56 (institution-wide framework) fits; the list is a preamble, not a rule.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded the list of considerations (privacy, compliance, copyright, academic integrity) separately; coder B folded it into the welcome unit. It names the principles of the framework, a distinct statement, so kept as P56 informs.
units.anchor: information security and data privacy, compliance, copyright, and academic integrity

units.why: 'USF is cautiously and judiciously exploring Generative Artificial Intelligence' states the institution's approach and purpose ('improve its operations, increase productivity and support learning'), so P56.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P56/informs/admin/general. Source: 'USF is cautiously and judiciously exploring Generative Artificial Intelligence ... as a means to improve its operations, increase productivity and support learning and instruction.' B's full normalization kept.
units.anchor: USF is cautiously and judiciously exploring Generative Artificial Intelligence
units.frag_start: USF is cautiously and judiciously exploring
units.frag_end: risks to data privacy and security.
units.policy: USF is cautiously and judiciously exploring Generative Artificial Intelligence as a means to improve its operations, increase productivity and support learning and instruction.

units.why: 'ill-conceived and rushed deployments may introduce risks to data privacy and security' warns about data privacy risk, which is P50 (protect data), as information.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded 'ill-conceived and rushed deployments may introduce risks to data privacy and security'; coder A used it only as rationale for the cautious-exploration unit. It states a distinct data-risk warning, kept as P50 informs.
units.anchor: ill-conceived and rushed deployments may introduce risks to data privacy and security

units.why: 'you must follow the University's Technology Resources Appropriate Use Policy, Information Security Policy, and Guidelines for Responsible Use' ties AI use to existing university policies (P77).

Source: 'you must follow the University's Technology Resources Appropriate Use Policy, Information Security Policy, and Guidelines for Responsible Use'. It binds AI use to existing policies but sets no position on AI use itself: neutral.

units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P50/must/all/restrict. They differed on phase (A general, B during-work). units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P63/informs/admin/before-course. Source: 'DLI offers a variety of classes to help faculty and staff develop their skills in GenAI.' A's fit note (covers staff as well) kept.

notes: The Guidelines for Responsible Use of AI at USF (usf.service-now.com KB15409) could not be fetched, so its content is not coded. Only two university-layer documents; no computing, school or course documents found or coded (course deferred). The syllabus page is a menu of templates, so its three options are coded as units under a delegates stance. Coder B units dropped on review as non-policy: the list of past events (P88), the list of other universities' guidance as references (P115), and the feedback email line (P54). Candidate type for review: warnings to instructors that bans are an equity issue (two UNCOVERED units: equity under bans, and caution about punishment when AI is embedded).
